nodes.label: The HANDOFF-13 collision and a fingerprint for an absent document
nodes.rationale: The gate certificate's HANDOFF-13 (9,463 B, 112 lines, md5 a07ad36d...) is a different document from the one recovered/ holds; the md5 appears in no ledger row. ABSENT, and not a loss — the certificate records it as a chat-uploaded copy never in the mirror.

nodes.label: tower-1-1.py and tower-2.py are byte-identical
nodes.rationale: The certificate's explicit non-measurement, now measured four ways at md5 c0bce27a..., retroactively validating a PASS that had checked behaviour rather than hash.

nodes.label: Ruling 41 exists because Ruling 28 was already executed
nodes.rationale: The standing prompt still carried a Phase 0-4 plan to perform an absorption BUILD90 had already seated; no sentence in the corpus names both rulings, which is why the edge could only be AMBIGUOUS.

nodes.label: The first-match fault family
nodes.rationale: Instruments that read a population and take what they reach first rather than what the population says — register 1578's object-versus-observer fault. Three members, one loudly false-negative, one manufacturing findings, one destructive.

nodes.label: A control must be proven to vary the thing it controls for
nodes.rationale: The corpus's own standing rule from F59.3, under which both instrument faults sit.

nodes.label: Co-membership on a parent neither endpoint names
nodes.rationale: A shape the corpus produces constantly — owed boards, gate certificates, deferral blocks, and a shared Register entry — and one a pairwise edge cannot express; the graph carries hyperedges for exactly this.

nodes.label: The dimensional obstruction
nodes.rationale: Scale separation of six orders in energy and five in length bars reasoning from configuration-space quantities to nuclear rates; upgrading either three-body edge above AMBIGUOUS would reproduce the error the corpus documents as its own worked negative result.

nodes.label: The truncation census — 23 files, 3,004 lines
nodes.rationale: A bounded, enumerated set: 22 of 23 have a complete copy in the repo, and completeness-outranks-recency put the complete body under the plain name.

nodes.label: HANDOFF-34 is the single hard boundary
nodes.rationale: Lines 34-42 missing with no complete copy anywhere; the marker is present twice in the source shard itself, so it is a boundary the chat export imposed and not a recovery defect.

nodes.label: The __<md5> suffix in recovered/ is not the __<driveFileId> convention
nodes.rationale: In recovered/ it is a disambiguator for two distinct bodies claiming one filename; the older/newer reading does not transfer, and two distinct shapes hide under it — the truncated re-posting and the genuine divergence.

nodes.label: The HANDOFF-26 governance divergence
nodes.rationale: Two complete bodies disagreeing on whether close.py may append to a seated member; the self-correction is in the earlier file and the later one is back to --append. Unreconciled by design.

nodes.label: The Lowdin bridge series — 63 of 66 held
nodes.rationale: Each bridge names its predecessor, so the spine reconstructs itself and the gaps are visible from inside the chain; absence measured against the repository is a statement about reach, not about the world.

nodes.label: The census of all 120 AMBIGUOUS edges
nodes.rationale: 0.33% of 36,150 links; 80 from images and 40 from text, of which 7 were the rebuild's questions and 5 sit inside one document. Only one was a fault in the repository rather than a limit of a pairwise edge.

nodes.label: The vision pass doubts at 38x the text rate
nodes.rationale: 4.6% of image-sourced edges are AMBIGUOUS against 0.12% from text, and every one of the 80 has both endpoints in the same figure — a measurement of the vision pass, not of the corpus, and not a candidate for tracing.

nodes.label: The handoff number space is used twice
nodes.rationale: 114 numbered handoff files under two numberings overlapping at 3-53: pre-restart is origin chat + 2, post-restart roughly origin chat - 48, and the corpus records a lineage fork at chats 52/53 merged at BUILD55. Nothing states one caused the other.

nodes.label: Six numbers where the wrong document answers
nodes.rationale: At 23, 25, 32, 33, 43 and 44 a citation resolves by filename to the other lineage's document; HANDOFF-45 cites a byte count HANDOFF-44 does not contain. Right about what is on disk, wrong about which document answers.

nodes.label: A house style makes unrelated documents read alike
nodes.rationale: 164 of 291 PREDICTION-/FINDING- files carry a pre-registration declaration; an extractor finds the same frame and vocabulary and cannot tell a relationship from a convention, so AMBIGUOUS is correct and the reason is the corpus's discipline.

nodes.label: --update is not usable here, and the reason is provenance
nodes.rationale: Extraction was clean and cached; the merge is the problem. 353 of 377 vanished nodes came from files that had not changed, 121 folding one tree into another, and the merged graph is smaller so the shrink guard refuses the write.

nodes.label: Which tree a body sits in is the finding about it
nodes.rationale: Collapsing a mirrored copy into a seated member is the same class of error as flattening RECOVERED-BY-WRITE to RECOVERED; a corpus with one source tree would take the merge happily and this one cannot.
